zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 5 (not a cabin deck), obstructing views from Decks 2, 3, 6, and 7, with Decks 2 and 3 most severely affected.
zones.effect: Oceanview and balcony cabins on these decks look directly at orange lifeboat shells instead of open water; the horizon remains visible above the boats.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to anyone wanting unobstructed ocean views; irrelevant to interior cabins or those who don't spend time looking out their window.

zones.what: The hull cantilevers outward past the lifeboat line starting at Deck 6, creating wider balconies in mid and aft sections on Decks 6, 7, and 8.
zones.effect: These balconies extend beyond the lifeboats for clearer side views and more balcony space, typically at lower prices than higher deck balconies.
zones.mattersTo: Value hunters wanting balconies with better views than the lifeboat-obstructed lower decks, and those who prefer midship stability over height.

zones.what: Pool deck (Deck 11 and 12 aft/mid) sits directly above or adjacent to cabins on Deck 11 and below cabins on Deck 12.
zones.effect: Daytime deck chair scraping, pool activity, and music from above until late evening; Deck 12 cabins may have limited overhang protection.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and anyone wanting quiet during pool hours (typically 8am-midnight) should avoid; doesn't affect those out exploring all day.

zones.what: The main showroom (theater) sits on Deck 3 and 4 forward, three to four decks below Deck 10 forward cabins.
zones.effect: No significant noise or vibration impact at this distance; showroom activity does not materially affect Deck 10 forward cabins.
zones.mattersTo: No concern for cabin selection; the vertical separation is sufficient.

zones.what: The Royal Promenade (interior boulevard with bars, cafes, and evening events) runs below on Deck 5, directly beneath Decks 6, 7, and 8 promenade-view interior cabins.
zones.effect: Promenade activity, music, parades, and foot traffic can be heard through the floor until 1-2am on event nights.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers should avoid promenade-view cabins; those wanting to be close to action or who sleep heavily won't mind.

zones.what: The sports deck and mini-golf area sit on Deck 13 forward, two decks above Deck 11 forward cabins.
zones.effect: Occasional ball bounce and footsteps during daytime and early evening sports activities.
zones.mattersTo: Minor annoyance for daytime nappers; most guests won't notice or will be elsewhere during activity hours.

zones.what: Engine rooms sit low and aft, directly below Deck 2 and 3 aft cabins.
zones.effect: Low-frequency vibration and hum, noticeable when the ship is underway, particularly during maneuvering.
zones.mattersTo: Anyone sensitive to vibration or low hum should avoid; those who sleep through anything or use white noise won't care.

zones.what: Bow thrusters are located low and forward, below and near Deck 2, 3, and 6 forward cabins.
zones.effect: Loud thruster rumble during docking and undocking (typically early morning arrival and evening departure), lasting 10-30 minutes per event.
zones.mattersTo: Very disruptive for early morning sleepers in forward cabins; doesn't affect mid or aft, and only happens during port maneuvers.

zones.what: Anchor chain runs through the bow area, affecting Deck 2 and 3 forward cabins.
zones.effect: Loud chain noise during anchor dropping and retrieval, typically early morning in tender ports.
zones.mattersTo: Disruptive for those anchoring in tender ports who want to sleep past 6-7am; irrelevant in dock-only itineraries.

zones.what: Elevator and stair banks are distributed forward, mid, and aft on all cabin decks, with major banks midship near the Royal Promenade access.
zones.effect: Cabins near elevators benefit from convenience but may hear doors, bell chimes, and hallway conversation; peak traffic during embarkation, meal times, and evening shows.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-limited guests prioritize proximity; light sleepers should request cabins away from elevator cores.

zones.what: The Windjammer buffet (Deck 11 forward) sits one to two decks above Deck 9 and 10 forward cabins.
zones.effect: Early morning buffet setup noise (chairs, carts, kitchen prep) starting around 6-6:30am, and foot traffic until late evening.
zones.mattersTo: Early risers won't mind; those wanting to sleep past 7am on sea days should avoid Deck 9 and 10 forward.
